- When sentiment is negative and prices are trending down, model tends to underpredict — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts too high — cap next-period forecast at 10–15% below peak to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is positive and prices are rising, model frequently overestimates — reduce forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often lags behind true price movements — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to capture momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price peaks in the second half — increase forecast from day 15 onward by 1–3% to account for lagged momentum.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes followed by recovery, model tends to underestimate recovery — add 2–4% to forecast in the 10–20 day window to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
